title: Verification of Truth Tables of Logic Gates Using Multisim
aim: To verify the truth tables of basic and universal digital logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) using Multisim / digital logic simulation.
apparatus_components: Interactive Digital Constants (0/1) and Digital Voltage Probes / Indicators
theory: Digital logic gates perform fundamental Boolean algebra operations on binary inputs (0 = LOW = 0 V, 1 = HIGH = 5 V TTL). AND outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1; OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1; NOT inverts its input; NAND and NOR are universal gates that invert AND and OR respectively; XOR outputs 1 when inputs differ (odd parity); XNOR outputs 1 when inputs are equal (even parity).
equations: XOR: Y = A ⊕ B = A'B + AB'
circuit_topology: Digital testbench driving 2-input gates (AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) and 1-input inverter (NOT) across all 4 binary input combinations (00, 01, 10, 11).
component_relationships: Inputs A, B -> Gate Input Pins (1, 2)
Gate Output Pin (3) -> Digital Probe / LED Indicator
simulation_type: Digital Truth-Table Verification across all 2^N binary states
procedure:
1. Place the logic gate IC (7408, 7432, 7404, 7400, 7402, 7486, or 74266) on the schematic.
2. Connect interactive digital switches for inputs A and B and a digital probe at output Y.
3. Toggle (A, B) through (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) and record output Y in the truth table.
result: The truth tables of all seven logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) were verified.
common_mistakes: Confusing XOR and XNOR truth table outputs for inputs (0,0) and (1,1)
Leaving TTL input pins floating instead of tying them to logic 0 or 1

viva_concepts.q: Why are NAND and NOR gates called universal gates?
viva_concepts.a: Because any Boolean function (NOT, AND, OR, XOR, etc.) can be implemented using only NAND gates or only NOR gates.

viva_concepts.q: Why is an XOR gate also called an inequality detector or odd-parity gate?
viva_concepts.a: Because its output is 1 if and only if its two inputs are unequal (01 or 10), which corresponds to an odd number of 1s.

viva_concepts.q: How do you make a NOT gate from a 2-input NAND or NOR gate?
viva_concepts.a: Tie both input terminals of the NAND (or NOR) gate together to the same input signal A, or tie one input of a NAND gate to logic 1.

viva_concepts.q: How many rows are in the truth table of an N-input logic gate?
viva_concepts.a: 2^N rows (4 rows for 2 inputs, 8 rows for 3 inputs).

viva_concepts.q: How areXOR and XNOR expressed in Python bitwise/boolean logic?
viva_concepts.a: XOR is `A ^ B`, and XNOR is `int(not (A ^ B))` or `int(A == B)`.

viva_concepts.q: What happens if a TTL 74xx gate input is left unconnected (floating)?
viva_concepts.a: A floating TTL input typically acts as a logic HIGH (1), which can cause unexpected truth table readings and noise pickup.

viva_concepts.q: If A = 1 and B = 0, what are the outputs of NAND, NOR, XOR, and XNOR?
Why must truth tables be generated by a deterministic Boolean engine rather than guessed by an LLM?
viva_concepts.a: Deterministic evaluation guarantees 100% accuracy for every minterm row without arithmetic or token hallucination.

viva_concepts.q: For which input combinations do OR and XOR produce different outputs?
viva_concepts.a: Only for (A=1, B=1), where OR outputs 1 and XOR outputs 0.

VERIFICATION OF TRUTH TABLES OF LOGIC GATES USING MULTISIM
Aim:
To verify the truth tables of basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR)
using Multisim.
Apparatus Required:
•

Computer with Multisim software installed

•

Digital input switches (Logic Toggles)

•

Digital output indicators (LEDs)

•

Basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR)

Procedure:
Open Multisim:
o

Launch the Multisim software on your computer.

Create a New Project:
o

Go to File > New > Project.

o

Name your project and click Create.

Place Logic Gates:
o

Go to the Place menu and select Component.

o

In the Select a component window, choose TTL as the family.

o

Select the desired logic gate (e.g., AND gate 7408, OR gate 7432, NOT gate
7404, etc.) and place them on the schematic workspace.

Add Inputs:
o

Place digital input switches (logic toggles) from the component library. These
will serve as the inputs to your logic gates.

o

Connect the inputs to the respective pins of the logic gates.

Add Outputs:
o

Place digital output indicators (LEDs) from the component library. These will
serve as the outputs to display the results of the logic gates.

o

Connect the outputs to the respective pins of the logic gates.

Connect Power Supply:
o

21 | P a g e

Ensure that your logic gates are connected to the necessary power supply.
Typically, for TTL logic gates, you will connect the Vcc and GND
appropriately.

Configure Inputs:
o

Set the initial states of the digital input switches to represent all possible
combinations of inputs (00, 01, 10, 11 for two-input gates).

Simulate the Circuit:
o

Run the simulation by clicking on the Run button.

o

Observe the output indicators (LEDs) for each combination of inputs and
record the results.

Verify Truth Table:
o

Compare the observed outputs with the expected truth table for each logic
gate.

code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Topology Classification: EXACT MANUAL TOPOLOGY (Verification of Truth Tables of Logic Gates (Experiment 7))
# 1. Run Digital Logic Truth Table Verification
print('=== DIGITAL TRUTH TABLE VERIFICATION ===')
rows = []
for idx in range(8):
    A, B, C = (idx >> 2) & 1, (idx >> 1) & 1, idx & 1
    sum_bit = A ^ B ^ C
    carry_bit = (A & B) | (B & C) | (A & C)
    sop_y = 1 if idx in (1, 3, 6) else 0
    rows.append((A, B, C, sum_bit, carry_bit, sop_y))
    print(f'A={A} B={B} C={C} | Sum={sum_bit} Carry={carry_bit} | SOP_Y={sop_y}')

# 2. Extract digital signals & 3. Plot digital timing waveforms
t = np.arange(8)
arr = np.array(rows)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(10, 7), sharex=True)
labels = ['Input A', 'Input B', 'Input C', 'Output Y']
cols = [0, 1, 2, 3 if 'ADDER' in 'LOGIC_GATES_TRUTH_TABLE' else 5]
for ax, col_idx, lbl in zip(axes, cols, labels):
    ax.step(t, arr[:, col_idx], where='post', linewidth=2)
    ax.set_ylabel(lbl)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.2, 1.2)
    ax.grid(True)
axes[0].set_title('Digital Logic Truth-Table Timing Waveforms')
axes[-1].set_xlabel('Input State Index (0..7)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('digital_truth_table_waveforms.png', dpi=150)
plt.show()
